answer: Each identity registers one shale-banked vine plot fed by glacier meltwater and locks a 75-credit bond, filing its vine row count and meter serial. The first fee is 36 credits; the k-th plot costs 36+8(k-1), so the 1000th costs 8028 and 1000 fakes pay 4,032,000 plus 75,000 locked. An auditor recomputes each water share from the glacier melt table and vine rows, burning the bond when a meter serial repeats under a second key or a row count mismatches. A rented-vine ring fails because one serial cannot water two key-bound plots. An honest grower pays 36 once and recovers the bond after audit.
